# Cross-cutting fit + build-custom

How the operator's stack interacts with hosting browser dev sessions, and the
build-custom alternative. Sources: [`citations.md`](../citations.md) [41]–[51].

## 1. Tailscale K8s Operator — exposing N session services

- **Ingress is HTTPS-only:** "Ingress resources only support TLS, and are only exposed
  over HTTPS using a MagicDNS name and publicly trusted certificates from Let's
  Encrypt"; "You must enable HTTPS and MagicDNS on your tailnet" [42]. With tailnet
  HTTPS deliberately disabled, **the Tailscale `Ingress` path is unavailable.**
- **LoadBalancer Service does plain HTTP:** a `type: LoadBalancer` +
  `loadBalancerClass: tailscale` Service exposes plain HTTP (no TLS) at
  `<name>.<tailnet>.ts.net` [42]. **This is the viable path** — one Service per session.
- **Proxy-pod cost / ProxyGroup:** default is "a tailnet device deployed as a
  `StatefulSet` with a single `Pod`" per exposed Service; a single Pod "may not be
  feasible for large installations (high resource consumption)" [41]. A pre-created
  multi-replica **ProxyGroup** lets you "expose many Service and Ingress resources …
  using a smaller number of proxy Pods" [42] — bounding pod count as sessions grow.

**Implication:** one `loadBalancerClass: tailscale` Service per session, bound to a
shared ProxyGroup → each session at its own HTTP `ts.net` hostname, bounded proxy
footprint, no TLS work. (WebSocket behaviour of code-server through LB Services at
concurrency is unverified — see gaps.)

## 2. Embedded-Tailscale coexistence (principle)

Two `tailscaled` instances on different pods are distinct tailnet identities and do not
conflict (the normal operator model). Any platform serving an HTTP dashboard + in-browser
terminal can sit behind the TS Operator and be reached browser-only with its embedded
mesh unused for that traffic — confirmed for Coder, whose browser path is server-relayed
HTTP [2]. The Coder subnet collision [6] only bites direct P2P, which browser use avoids.

## 3. Longhorn RWO per-session

RWO is the right per-session primitive. The Multi-Attach hazard is real: "The volume …
cannot be attached to the node worker-5 since it is already attached to the node
worker-6" when a pod reschedules before the old attachment releases; **RollingUpdate
triggers it** [43]. Fix by construction: model each session as a **StatefulSet
(replicas: 1)** with `volumeClaimTemplates` — ordered termination releases the RWO
volume before the replacement attaches [50] — never a Deployment with RollingUpdate on
an RWO PVC. Stop/start and node-drain then work (Longhorn replicas live on multiple
nodes; the volume detaches and reattaches on the new node).

## 4. Argo CD managing the platform vs platform-managed sessions

The "Argo CD installs the platform; the platform/portal creates sessions outside Argo
CD" pattern is correct: "If the tracking annotation does not reference the resource it
is applied to, the resource will neither affect the application's sync status nor be
marked for pruning" [45] — dynamically created session pods/PVCs (no tracking-id) are
invisible to sync/prune. The one gotcha is **Orphaned Resources Monitoring**, which is
**warn-only** and excludable by Group/Kind/Name [44]. Cleanest boundary: run sessions in
a **dedicated namespace** no Argo Application manages.

## 5. Anthropic OAuth credential model (highest-risk)

- Storage: Linux `~/.claude/.credentials.json` mode `0600`, **no keychain** (PVC-
  portable); honors `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; precedence `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` >
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` > `apiKeyHelper` > `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` > subscription `/login`
  [46].
- **Headless auto-refresh is broken.** Cloudflare WAF blocks the OAuth refresh POST from
  headless Linux (403 → 429): "Token expires → refresh blocked → permanent lockout";
  reporter locked out 26 days (filed Apr 14 2026) [47]. Refresh tokens are single-use, so
  **concurrent sessions sharing one `.credentials.json` invalidate each other** [48
  (#24317)]. Copied creds yield 401 rather than refreshing (#21765, closed not-planned)
  [51].
- **Consequences for any platform:** (a) per-session **isolated** `~/.claude` PVC is
  mandatory — never share credentials across sessions [48]; (b) the operator's
  sidecar-re-run-`claude`-to-refresh pattern is fragile under the Cloudflare block [47];
  (c) the **reliable headless path is `claude setup-token`** → a one-year
  `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` injected per session via a Secret [46], accepting an annual
  manual rotation. Note the Jun 15 2026 Agent SDK credit change for `claude -p`/SDK usage
  [46] (interactive sessions are the normal case here).

This model is **platform-agnostic** — it applies equally to Coder, Che, JupyterHub,
kube-coder, or build-custom, since all permit a per-session PVC + Secret/sidecar.

## 6. Build-custom design + precedents

- **Per-session** = StatefulSet (replicas: 1) + RWO PVC running **code-server** (its
  integrated terminal *is* the terminal — no separate ttyd needed) with `claude`
  installed; initContainer clones the config repo; sidecar/Secret supplies the
  `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` [50][46].
- **Exposure** = one `loadBalancerClass: tailscale` Service per session on a shared
  ProxyGroup → `http://<session>.<tailnet>.ts.net` [42].
- **Portal** = **Headlamp** (browser k8s UI: pod exec, scale replicas, restart/delete,
  RBAC-aware) covers browser-only start (scale 0→1) / stop (1→0) / exec with zero custom
  code [49]; or a ~200–400-line k8s-API web app for a friendlier list/launch UX.
- **GitOps** = Argo CD manages the chart; sessions live in an unmanaged namespace [44][45].
- **Precedent:** kube-coder already implements most of this (per-user code-server RWO pod
  + Claude Code + browser terminal + OAuth) [32] — adopt or fork it rather than greenfield.

## 7. Counter-perspective (overkill vs adopt)

Pro-build: workspace platforms target dev *teams*; a single operator pays a multi-tenancy
tax (Coder's external Postgres + Terraform + mesh; Che's ~13 GiB control plane [10]) for
features never used. Pro-adopt: a hand-rolled portal can creep into a half-baked control
plane; adopting gives templates, isolation, lifecycle for free. **Mitigation that
resolves the tension:** use Headlamp (don't write a portal) + dumb StatefulSets +
kube-coder as a reference — caps custom surface to a Helm chart + a credential sidecar.

## Gaps / limitations

- WebSocket reliability of code-server through `loadBalancerClass: tailscale` LB Services
  at concurrency: unverified.
- No hard numeric ceiling on Services per ProxyGroup ("limited by resource consumption").
- Headlamp exec/scale specifics and StatefulSet ordered-termination are Snippet-level
  (consistent with docs, not re-fetched verbatim here).
